# `docs/figures/archive/` — figures a standard pipeline run cannot reproduce

**Archived 12.08.2026 (Selin).** Nothing here is current, and nothing here can be regenerated by
running the pipeline as it now stands. They are kept because they were cited, not because they hold.

The rule that put them here: **a figure that can only be produced from a target the pipeline no
longer writes, or from a training run that no longer exists, is not reproducible — so it is archived
rather than rendered.** `make_figures.py` skips each of them with a printed reason instead of
building them from whatever happens to be on disk. A figure that renders anyway is worse than one
that is absent, because nothing on its face says which target it came from.

> ✅ **Updated 14.08.2026 — two of the four below now build again, and the table is no longer
> accurate about the other two.**
>
> `figure_data.npz` was the common blocker: it was archived as un-rebuildable because it came from the
> retired `auc` target. That target's replacement has since been produced, so `make_figures.py`
> rebuilt the cache from `auc_cc` and it now sits at the live path again (the archived copy here is
> the void-era one and is untouched).
>
> * **`loss_02_weights.png` — builds.** Its blocker was the cache alone.
> * **`loss_03_effect.png` — builds**, after `panel_corr()` was repointed from this archive onto
>   `outputs/panel/` and migrated from the retired `weighted` column to `alpha`.
> * **`pipeline.png` and `model_architecture.png` — still skip, but not for the reason below.**
>   The cache is no longer missing. What remains is `EXAMPLE_PRED`: eight out-of-fold predictions
>   from the **void 8-drug panel**, drawn against the rebuilt 11-drug panel's names, so every bar
>   would carry another compound's name. Out-of-fold predictions for the rebuilt panel now exist,
>   so this is repairable — but refreshing that vector changes what the figures show, so it is
>   Selin's call rather than a mechanical fix.

| File | Why it cannot be regenerated |
|---|---|
| `figure_data.npz` | The cache every panel below is derived from. Built on the retired **`auc`** target and the **void 8-drug panel**, so it is 8 columns wide. `figure_data()` now reads `auc_cc` only — and that h5ad has never been written, because preprocessing has not re-run under the [freeze](../../TODO.md). |
| `pipeline.png` | Needs the cache *and* the panel CSVs. |
| `model_architecture.png` | Needs the cache: its per-drug bars are out-of-fold predictions for one cell line. |
| `loss_02_weights.png` | Needs the cache: it plots one drug's label density and the weight curve fitted to it. |
| `loss_03_effect.png` | Different reason, and the harder one. Its input is a **training output** — per-drug correlations from the 27.07.2026 run — so it cannot be rebuilt by re-reading an h5ad at all; it needs a re-run. The rebuilt panel shares only 3 of its 11 drugs with that run, so it would otherwise plot three points and read as a complete comparison. |

**What still builds, and why.** `pipeline_overview.png` and `loss_01_objective.png` are pure
drawings — they read no data — so they are always reproducible and stay in
[`docs/figures/`](../).

**When these come back.** At **R4** of the sweep, once stages 1 and 3 have written the `auc_cc`
h5ad and stage 4 has trained on the rebuilt panel. At that point `make_figures.py` rebuilds the
cache from `auc_cc`, every skip clears by itself, and these five are deleted rather than restored —
what replaces them will be computed on a different target and a different panel, so they are not
earlier versions of the same figures.

The panel itself is no longer duplicated in `make_figures.py`: `PANEL` is read from
`notebooks/outputs/panel/panel.csv`, which is what let this drift go unnoticed — the panel was
rebuilt on 12.08.2026 and the hardcoded copy was not.
